# Button

A control that commits an action on this screen.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Accessible first</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-button--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:accessible-first" title="Button examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-button--docs">Open Button in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-button--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:accessible-first;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Accessible first:** Every action, with a large target.

- **Use it when:** The press does something here: save, submit, delete, open a dialog, go to the next step.
- **Not when:** The press only takes people to another page, or flips a setting that should persist.

Instead:

- [Toggle](./toggle.md): An on or off setting that should persist as state.
- Link: Navigation to another page or section.

## Why it works this way

Button looks the way it does because of 7 answers about this product. Each card is one answer, in three steps: the answer, what it decided for Button, and what would move if it changed.

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-color-count"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How many emphasis levels do actions need?</b><code>color.count</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Two</div><p>Primary and secondary only; fewer choices, fewer errors.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>primary</b>: The one next step on a page.</span></li></ul></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Button decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-human-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>How do people recall the interface?</b><code>human.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">They see it fresh each time</div><p>Nobody remembers the interface from last time.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>secondary</b>: Every other action, always with a word: alternatives, row actions, and the first step of a delete.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>ghost</b>: Every action looks like a button people can find.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>disabled</b>: Keep it enabled and explain on press: nobody is left out, and nobody remembers the interface from last time.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Field: responsive</code> <code>Toggle: default</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">4</div><small>Button decisions would reopen</small><p>and 1 answer that follow from it: <b>Actions and status</b>.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-outcomes-q2"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is a costly mistake?</b><code>outcomes.q2</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">A task that fails</div><p>A failed form can cost someone a benefit.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>secondary</b>: Every other action, always with a word: alternatives, row actions, and the first step of a delete.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Alert: destructive</code> <code>Badge: warning</code> <code>Badge: danger</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Button decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-accessibility-values"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What is the smallest target?</b><code>accessibility.values</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Large</div><p>Large targets for tremor and touch.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="y">✓</span><span>uses <b>default</b>: Every button. Large targets help people with motor needs.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>compact</b>: Large targets help people with motor needs; nothing smaller.</span></li><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>large</b>: The default size is already large for motor needs; a bigger one adds nothing.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Toggle: default</code> <code>Toggle: sm</code> <code>Toggle: lg</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">3</div><small>Button decisions would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="odv-trail" id="why-iconography-roles"><div class="odv-trail-head"><b>What do icons do?</b><code>iconography.roles</code></div><div class="odv-steps"><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>1</i>The answer</h5><div class="odv-answer">Actions and status</div><p>Icons support words; they never replace them.</p></div><div class="odv-step-col"><h5><i>2</i>So Button</h5><ul><li><span class="n">–</span><span>does not use <b>icon</b>: Icons alone are guesswork: always add a word.</span></li></ul><div class="odv-also"><small>It also shapes</small> <code>Input group: inline-end</code> <code>Toggle: outline</code></div></div><div class="odv-step-col change"><h5><i>3</i>If it changed</h5><div class="odv-big">1</div><small>Button decision would reopen</small><p>No other answer follows from it.</p></div></div></section>

## Words

- Use common words. Explain any term you must use.
- One idea per sentence. Put the action first.
- Never blame the person.
- Use: Continue, Change, Start, You. Avoid: Invalid, Utilise, Submit, Error code.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Continue
- `content.action.cancel`: Go back
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Start a new application

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Moving through the page or a dialog. | Tab lands on the button in a logical order. | The control is skipped because it used HTML disabled. |
| The button is focused and the person confirms. | Enter runs the same action as a click. | Enter only works on submit buttons. |
| The button is focused. | Space runs the same action as a click. | Space scrolls the page instead. |
| The button opened a dialog, menu or popover that just closed. | After the action closes a surface, focus returns to the button. | Focus dropped on the page body. |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] The control has a name assistive tech can speak. Any button, especially an icon-only one.
- [ ] The focused control stays visible; color alone is not the cue. Keyboard or assistive-tech focus is on the button.
- [ ] Unavailable stays in the tab order and explains why. The action must not run, but focus must not jump away.
- [ ] A button that stays down exposes its pressed state. Pin, follow, or another sticky on or off on a button.
- [ ] A button that opens something exposes open or closed. The press reveals a menu, panel or more content.
- [ ] The hit area stays usable, including at a small size. Touch, pointer, or a compact toolbar button.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add button
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Component keys

The CSS variable is the key with `/` replaced by `-` and the base `@` dropped. Each key points to a token; values live only on primitives.

| Key | What it controls | Points to, light | Points to, dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `button/primary/background/@` | Primary button fill. | `color.action.primary.@` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.action.primary.@` → `color.blue.light.600` | `color.action.primary.@` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.action.primary.@` → `color.blue.dark.700` |
| `button/primary/background/hover` | Primary button fill on hover. | `color.action.primary.hover` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.action.primary.hover` → `color.blue.light.700` | `color.action.primary.hover` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.action.primary.hover` → `color.blue.dark.800` |
| `button/primary/label` | Primary button label color. | `color.text.on-action` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.text.on-action` → `color.gray.light.0` | `color.text.on-action` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.text.on-action` → `color.gray.dark.0` |
| `button/secondary/background/@` | Secondary button fill. | `color.action.secondary.@` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.action.secondary.@` → `color.gray.light.0` | `color.action.secondary.@` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.action.secondary.@` → `color.gray.dark.50` |
| `button/secondary/background/hover` | Secondary button fill on hover. | `color.action.secondary.hover` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.action.secondary.hover` → `color.gray.light.100` | `color.action.secondary.hover` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.action.secondary.hover` → `color.gray.dark.100` |
| `button/secondary/label` | Secondary button label color. | `color.text.primary` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.text.primary` → `color.gray.light.900` | `color.text.primary` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.text.primary` → `color.gray.dark.900` |
| `button/secondary/border` | Secondary button border. | `color.border.strong` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.border.strong` → `color.gray.light.500` | `color.border.strong` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.border.strong` → `color.gray.dark.400` |
| `button/ghost/background-hover` | Ghost button fill on hover. | `color.surface.sunken` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.surface.sunken` → `color.gray.light.100` | `color.surface.sunken` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.surface.sunken` → `color.gray.dark.100` |
| `button/ghost/label` | Ghost button label color. | `color.text.link` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.text.link` → `color.blue.light.700` | `color.text.link` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.text.link` → `color.blue.dark.700` |
| `button/height` | Button height. | `size.control.default` → `size.52` | same |
| `button/padding-x` | Horizontal padding inside a button. | `space.inset.control-x` → `space.24` | same |
| `button/radius` | Button corner radius. | `radius.control` → `accessible-first.theme.base.radius.control` → `radius.6` | same |
| `button/font-size` | Button label size. | `type.label.font-size` → `font.size.18` | same |
| `button/font-weight` | Button label weight. | `type.label.font-weight` → `font.weight.700` | same |
| `button/focus-ring` | Focus ring color on any button. | `color.border.focus` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.border.focus` → `color.blue.light.600` | `color.border.focus` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.border.focus` → `color.blue.dark.700` |
| `button/icon-size` | Size of an icon inside a button. | `size.icon` → `size.20` | same |
| `button/disabled/background` | Fill of a disabled button. | `color.disabled.surface` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.disabled.surface` → `color.gray.light.100` | `color.disabled.surface` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.disabled.surface` → `color.gray.dark.100` |
| `button/disabled/label` | Label of a disabled button. | `color.disabled.text` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.disabled.text` → `color.gray.light.500` | `color.disabled.text` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.disabled.text` → `color.gray.dark.500` |
| `button/disabled/border` | Border of a disabled secondary button. | `color.disabled.border` → `accessible-first.theme.light.color.disabled.border` → `color.gray.light.200` | `color.disabled.border` → `accessible-first.theme.dark.color.disabled.border` → `color.gray.dark.200` |
